p8_b0.ocr: The following data table presents a comparative analysis of surgical outcomes between two distinct intervention arms and their control counterparts, with a focus on abdominal and vaginal surgery. Specifically, the table outlines the percentage of patients undergoing abdominal surgery (n = 37) and vaginal surgery (n = 31) across the respective arms. The intervention arm demonstrates a notable difference in surgical success rates, which correlates with the estimated number of live births in the targeted area, reported at 3,603 for the intervention group and 3,439 for the control group.

p8_b1.ocr: Additionally, the p value serves as a critical metric in assessing the statistical significance of the observed differences, further elucidating the efficacy of the intervention. The importance of anesthesia as a contributing factor to surgical outcomes is also highlighted in the analysis, underscoring the need for optimized protocols to enhance birth outcomes in clinical settings. This table thus provides valuable insights into the effectiveness of different surgical approaches and their implications for maternal and neonatal health within the intervention area.
